intent: Increased sensor size from 0.012 to 0.016 to improve noise robustness and line detection stability, as suggested by integrator feedback. Shifted sensor y-positions forward by 0.01 to detect the line earlier and enhance control anticipation. Increased wheel track from 0.14 to 0.16 to improve turning stability and reduce steering oscillation. These changes aim to reduce line loss events and steering oscillations observed in previous races, improving overall line following performance and control smoothness.
learning: Request telemetry on completion, progress, rms_error, line_loss_events, and steering_oscillation to verify if increased sensor size and forward sensor placement improve line detection and control anticipation. Also monitor if wider wheel track reduces steering oscillation and line loss events. These measurements will confirm if the geometry changes enhance robustness and smoothness as intended.
rationale: Integrator feedback and race telemetry indicate line loss events and steering oscillations likely due to sensor coverage and robot stability. Increasing sensor size enhances noise robustness and line detection reliability. Moving sensors forward allows earlier line detection, aiding anticipatory control. A wider wheel track improves turning stability, reducing oscillations. These targeted geometry adjustments address observed weaknesses and are expected to improve completion rates and reduce errors on both oval and s-bend tracks, supporting better generalization.
